how: Locates initiation in the member proposing a missing national flag and asking others to build it together.
Connects the missing flag to calls for collective construction, rebuilding, and defense.
Makes proposed expansion contingent on available people, their hours, and the effort required for an additional design.

statement: explaining how the shared canvas works
how: Explains timed pixel changes and collective construction or destruction to participants who do not understand the canvas.
Builds national representation through the flag and Hangul while adjusting character shapes to a constrained pixel space.
Adds a separate Korean heart and identifies the outside contributors credited with the adjacent Seolhyun heart.
Makes construction visible through reports of a completed circle, a character being made, and the part currently being placed.
Uses a selected template and a posted flag reference to orient construction.
Requires compatible uptake because participants can undo one another's corrections even while treating their own pixels as repairs.
Explains how invitations to help and claims of earlier labor become competing entitlements to label the shared flag.
Shows invited contributors' help being invoked as a reason they deserve space within the representation they helped sustain.
Accepts a proposed character with a bare commitment to make it.
Volunteered tasks show local coordination but cannot test cross-room prevalence or exclude decisions outside these exchanges.
Scattered work and difficulty maintaining pixels do not identify scripts or spare accounts or establish their nonuse.
Keeps the placed flag through trigram maintenance, repairs, and requests to answer rapid vandalism.
Separates a claimed invasion from an answering account blaming griefers on both sides.
Responds to a blacked-out character by proposing private contact with an individual placer, whose answer remains unseen.
Answers losing or unholdable positions with replacement locations and agreement that having a flag matters more than its site.
Returns an invaded attempt to construction through replacement coordinates, their acceptance, and an explicit report of joining there.
Answers a neighbour's request to stop overlapping with an explicit agreement to coexist.
Rejects signing the flag by writing over another group's existing work.
Distinguishes negotiation motivated by an organized neighbour's resistance from restraint grounded in reluctance to overwrite others.
Turns a reported refusal into suggestions for swapping territory or relocating and rebuilding the neighbour's work.
Carries a screenshot-based request to the neighbouring room and relays its proposal to write around the heart.
Permission-seeking to overlay a heart leads to writing around it without establishing a completed guest work under host government.
Relays requests between rooms and plans to circulate a design for additional helpers.
Credit to outside helpers does not identify a coalition joined by the host room.
Ownership and contributor-credit disputes do not themselves contest an envoy's authority to bind every placer to an agreement.
Extends the picture dispute into arguments about Korean ethnicity, diaspora belonging, and whether K-pop counts as heritage.
Keeps reciprocal tests of belonging and competing definitions visible without converting the unresolved exchange into a shared membership rule.
Historical analogies in a canvas dispute do not establish an organized quarrel carried over from before the event.
The attack call names a national target, but the historical analogy appears in another turn rather than supplying its same-turn reason.
Stages false headlines, reveals their April Fools status, and receives admissions of belief and challenges to plausibility.
Answers complaints about repeated canvas submissions by limiting planning to one moderator thread.
Sets comments to new so fresh planning stays findable within the single permitted discussion thread.
Distinguishes interception by a general low-karma rule from event-specific decisions to contain canvas talk.
Contests the canvas's value through accusations of wasted time and replies defending collective participation.
Marks provisional success and later credits members and outside helpers for the surviving images.
Allows celebration of a standing work while its survival remains uncertain and maintenance continues.
Records survival through reports that the flag is untouched and the final images remain intact.
Closing reports describe survival without documenting a successor effort or an enduring institution.
Intact-result reports and a continuing heritage dispute do not document contention over a cleaned or authoritative preserved canvas copy.
Turns national flag construction toward proposals to convert the neighbouring country's flag.
Proposes erasing another group's lettering to enlarge or relabel the national work without establishing that the overwrite occurred.
Carries the flag dispute into a taunting historical analogy and a direct reply mocking its equation with colonisation.
Connects the flag call to explicit joining and later reporting of a completed component without inferring silent readers' placement.
Treats initiating and calling as simultaneous when the member proposes the flag and recruits helpers in the same opening.
Shows a completed component immediately generating filling and cleanup tasks, with upkeep recurring after celebration.
Supports a suggestion to recruit or negotiate over border pressure, rather than a demonstrated completed negotiation caused by maintenance.
The coexistence request and assent do not document later restraint caused by compliance with a settled border.
Manual maintenance strain and abandoned expansion do not document a transition to machines or prove machines unnecessary.
Connects reported construction to provisional success and collective celebration while preserving continuing repair work.
An edited opener combines celebration and final-state recording without dating the edit or establishing that celebration caused recording.
Survival reports do not document a subsequent decision to preserve an organization, emblem, or future activity.
Makes the judgment that a position cannot be kept an explicit reason to propose a different site.
Requires agreement in uptake because reference designs coexist with incompatible corrections and requests to restore a different version.
Shows a proposed character receiving a bare commitment, while the original collective call also attracts a reasoned refusal.
Strain, recruitment suggestions, and retrospective thanks do not establish a specific causal chain from insufficient hands to received outside placement.
Shows separate-claim negotiation accompanied by offers of help and an answering agreement to work together.
Shows a cooperative flag call receiving a takeover proposal and target-selection reply.
Answers a takeover call with a direct refusal grounded in avoiding conflict.
Answers a takeover proposal with the targeted room's request that each side keep its own claim.
Shows the flag takeover carried into a historical taunt and a direct challenge to the analogy.
Acknowledged outside help does not document joining a coalition in response to maintenance threats.
Connects repeated event submissions and complaints about their volume to the moderator's explicit containment of planning in one thread.
Negotiation and ownership disagreement do not show members disputing whether an agreement binds all placers.
